decisions.issues: v07 is the only candidate. It gets most of the beat right. The Woman (grey-streaked loose knot, undyed cotton) wrings a cloth into a basin while she speaks sharply. The Fisherman (red lungi, cream vest, shoulder cloth, as in 6.2 and 6.3) relays with a half smile. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, chin clean apart from light stubble, gold stud in his left ear, loose curly hair, bare-chested with the chest rope burns seen in 5.5. There is no text or gore, and the wide plain wall across the upper half leaves plenty of room for both FISHERMAN balloons. It fails on the brand. His torso faces the camera, so the arm coming from the image-left shoulder is his RIGHT arm, and that forearm has a large puckered, ridged burn patch near the elbow, just above the bandage. That is the brand drawn on the wrong arm and in the wrong place. The bible puts it on the inner LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, and the Woman stares at it there in 5.4 and the kapitan weighs it in 6.5, so a second brand on the right arm is a visible continuity error. Smaller problems: the basin is a wooden stave tub, not the round clay basin from 5.5 in the same scene. The Woman's white garment has short sleeves that read like a blouse under the drape, which breaks 'no fitted blouse'. The room (clay hearth at left, bare round mud wall) is barer than the 5.5 interior.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: a wide interior, the Woman seated at left wringing the cloth over the basin, the Fisherman sitting between them with a half smile and an open-hand relaying gesture, Nagoji reclining on the woven mat in the right foreground with his head turned toward them, and the broad plain wall across the upper half left empty for lettering. Fix the arms: Nagoji's RIGHT arm (the one nearer the Woman and the Fisherman) must show smooth unmarked skin from elbow to bandaged wrist, with no burn, scar, brand or puckered patch anywhere on it. His LEFT forearm should either lie turned away from camera or be tucked under the cream dhoti so no brand shows in this panel; if any brand appears, it must be only on the inner side of the LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist. Make the basin the same wide, round, unglazed terracotta clay basin as in the previous panel, not a wooden tub or barrel. Dress the Woman in coarse undyed cotton worn sari-fashion with the end drawn over both shoulders and bare forearms, with no sleeves, no blouse and no stitched garment.
